what_its_for: Tolterodine is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, how often you need to urinate, and accidental leaks of urine. It works by relaxing the bladder muscle so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Take tolterodine by mouth with or without food. Swallow the extended-release capsules (Detrol LA) whole — do not crush, chew, or open them. The regular tablets (Detrol) are usually taken twice a day. The extended-release capsules are taken once a day. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose of the regular tablet is 2 mg twice a day. Your doctor may lower this to 1 mg twice a day if you have side effects. The extended-release capsule is usually 4 mg once a day, which may be lowered to 2 mg once a day. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tolterodine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol while taking tolterodine, as it can increase dizziness and drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medication affects you, since it can cause blurred vision or dizziness. Try to avoid becoming overheated or dehydrated in hot weather, as tolterodine can reduce sweating and raise your body temperature. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medications you take, especially antifungal medicines like ketoconazole or fluconazole, certain antibiotics, or other bladder medications, as these can interact with tolterodine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: difficulty urinating or cannot urinate at all, severe stomach pain or constipation, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing, fast or irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness or confusion, eye pain or sudden vision changes, or signs of heat stroke such as hot dry skin, high fever, or not sweating. Also contact your doctor if your overactive bladder symptoms do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your symptoms within 1 to 2 weeks of starting tolterodine. However, it may take up to 4 to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medication. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate results. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older) may be more sensitive to the side effects of tolterodine, especially confusion, dizziness, and urinary retention, so use with caution and report any new symptoms to your doctor. People with liver or kidney problems may need a lower dose — make sure your doctor knows about any liver or kidney issues before you start this medication. Tolterodine is not approved for use in children. If you are pregnant or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using tolterodine, as its safety during pregnancy and breastfeeding has not been fully established.
